I build the infrastructure that turns promising technical capabilities into dependable products: evaluation, data contracts, observability, and the tools that help teams ship.

## Work

At [Woven by Toyota](https://woven.toyota/en/), I was one of the founding engineers of MS1, a B2B product focused on talent mobility. I helped build its data infrastructure, skill-intelligence systems, adaptive assessments, course recommendations, talent matching, and cloud foundations.

I now lead the ML and Data Platform team. Our work spans production ML and AI infrastructure, data orchestration, model evaluation, developer experience, platform reliability, privacy, and governance. My role combines hands-on architecture with technical leadership: deciding what the platform should own and helping engineers and data scientists build on it.

Previously, at [BookMyShow](https://bookmyshow.com), I built real-time data and discovery infrastructure used to personalize entertainment experiences for millions of users. Earlier work included distributed databases, consensus systems, and education products.

## What I’m exploring

I’m interested in how systems preserve evidence, make state visible, and give people meaningful control. Those questions connect my work on AI evaluation, memory, data platforms, and distributed systems.

In [The Evaluation Machine](/posts/evaluation-systems/), I examine the contracts and evidence that let teams decide whether learned behavior is ready to ship. [Rocketships for the Mind](/posts/from-search-to-memory/) describes a system I built to recover project state and construct useful memory from 6,604 AI conversations.

I also publish [interactive research at Novus Opus](https://www.novusopus.org/research/), where readers can explore ideas through simulations and experiments. The full collection is in [Writing](/posts/).

## Background

I studied computer science at IIT Indore. Open resources such as [MIT OpenCourseWare](https://ocw.mit.edu/) and the [Linux Documentation Project](https://tldp.org/) shaped my belief that technical knowledge becomes more valuable when it is understandable and shared openly. This website is my contribution to that tradition.

Outside work, I read across technology, business, economics, history, and science. You can explore my [Library](https://www.arjunsriva.com/library/) or listen to [Byte-Sized Breakthroughs](/podcast/), my collection of AI-generated research-paper conversations. I also love biryani, Mexican food, barbecue, swimming, and skating.

I enjoy hearing from people building ambitious systems in ML, data, developer infrastructure, search, and memory. [Get in touch](mailto:arjunsriva@gmail.com), or [subscribe to new essays on Substack](https://arjunsriva.substack.com/).
